findings.description: Any fork PR author can set off a full recompute of every open PR at will: each title edit runs "Label PRs" (`pull_request_target`, never skipped), and that run ends in pr-status's recompute-all. The shared `'all'` group only makes these runs line up one after another, so a loop of title edits keeps the job busy without a break.
findings.body:
**The comment-flood fix leaves one outsider trigger open: "Label PRs"**

This delta skips `workflow_run` events whose conclusion is `skipped`, and puts the recompute-all runs in one shared group. That closes the issue-comment route. One trigger an outsider controls still passes the guard and always recomputes every PR:

```yaml
workflow_run:
  workflows: ["Claude Code Review", "Label PRs"]
  types: [completed]
```

- **Label PRs runs for anyone.** `labeler.yml` runs on `pull_request_target: types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, edited]` (L11), and its `label` job has no `if` (L17-19). Every title edit, including one by a fork PR author, therefore concludes `success` and gets past the new `conclusion != 'skipped'` check (L44).
- **Its runs link no PR.** A `pull_request_target` run's head is the base branch, and GitHub never lists fork PRs in `pull_requests` (medium confidence: platform behavior). The group falls back to `'all'` (L38), and the script recomputes every open PR. Its own comment says so (L64): `// Empty for a run on main (an \`@claude review\` retry, Label PRs): recompute them all.`
- **The cost still adds up.** Each run makes 6 `createLabel` calls and one `pulls.list`. Per open PR it adds 1-5 `pulls.get` (with up to 12 s of sleep), `listReviews`, `getCombinedStatusForRef`, `checks.listForRef`, `listLabelsOnIssue` and the label writes. That is about 60-100 calls with 10 open PRs. The shared group collapses a burst to one running and one pending run, but one edit per run keeps a fresh run queued. Running back to back like that goes well past the repo's 1,000 requests/hour `GITHUB_TOKEN` limit, which the review preflight and poster also draw from for their `claude-review` statuses.

`edited` was already in `labeler.yml` at the merge base. The route opened when this PR added `"Label PRs"` to `workflow_run.workflows`.

**Possible fix.** A title edit cannot change the `pr/*` status, and pr-status already runs on the same `pull_request_target` events (minus `edited`). So drop `"Label PRs"` from `workflow_run.workflows` and from the header comment, and ignore its check run instead:

```js
).filter((c) => c.name !== context.job && c.name !== "label" && !contexts.has(c.name));
```

(`label` is the job id in `labeler.yml`. Like the `context.job` filter, it has to change if that job ever gets a `name:`.)

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/a0e20d80f8d130437bcc424e1739673556720902/.github/workflows/pr-status.yml#L61-L70

findings.description: If someone asks for `@claude review` on a head the preflight marked comment-only, the review runs on main (`issue_comment`). The only signal on the head is then the pending "Not reviewed" status, which no longer counts as running, so the PR shows `pr/ready` for the whole review run (up to 40 min). Before this delta it showed `pr/ci-pending`.

`startsWith("Not reviewed")` hard-codes text the preflight's `markNotReviewed` (`tools/review/src/review-preflight.script.ts:204`) writes, and `src/core/ci-wait.service.ts:31` (`COMMENT_ONLY_STATUS`) already matches it separately. Neither side names the other, so a wording change silently brings back the permanent `pr/ci-pending`. The prefix is also broader than the comment-only case the comment describes. Match the full `Not reviewed: only comments and prose changed` prefix, and point at the producer.

A linked `workflow_run` with several PRs joins only the group of `pull_requests[0]`. If it is still pending when a newer event for that PR arrives, GitHub cancels it, and the other linked PRs miss their recompute until their next event. This is rare: it needs two PRs open from the same head branch.

A recompute-all run (group `pr-status-all`) and a per-PR run (group `pr-status-N`) can relabel the same PR at the same time, for example a push to main during a PR event. Each reads the labels and then removes and adds. If both read before either writes, the PR ends up with two `pr/*` labels, or an older computed status overwrites a newer one, until the next event. The delta narrows this race (recompute-all runs no longer race each other, and linked runs now share the PR's group) but does not close it.

`startup_failure` is a workflow-run conclusion, not a check-run conclusion, so this entry in the `bad` set can never match a check run. It is harmless, but `stale` is the only addition that does anything.
